prior_claim: Nothing regrows heart muscle; nobody has replaced it in a human.
search_finding: FALSE. Jebran et al. Nature 2025;639:503-511 examined an explanted human heart 3 months after EHM implantation and found retained, vascularised, viable graft. BioVAT-HF (NEJM 2026, NEJMoa2513525): 16 patients at 20 EHM units / 800M iPSC-CMs, target wall +4.5 mm and LVEF +3.9 pp at 3 months, +6.9 pp at mean 17 months. No graft-related arrhythmia or tumour.
solution: Stop asking whether remuscularisation is possible and ask how to reach +20 pp. Two levers, both from the same human data: mass scaling needs 5.13x the demonstrated dose at 3 months, but maturation alone lifts the effect 1.77x and cuts the mass requirement to 2.90x. Because wall thickness FELL (4.5 to 2.9 mm) while LVEF ROSE (3.9 to 6.9 pp), maturation and mechanical entrainment look like the real lever. Protocol: randomise maximal-dose EHM recipients to standard versus maturation-optimised grafts (longer in-vitro conditioning, paced load training) and follow to 24 months, with the existing patch as active control.
primary_endpoint: change in LVEF by cardiac MRI at 24 months, active-controlled
blockers: Lifelong immunosuppression; epicardial surface area limits coverage; vascularisation depth; open-label uncontrolled precedent with n=16 and surrogate endpoints; 196 AEs / 57 serious in 20 patients.
falsifier: If LVEF gain does not keep rising after 12 months, maturation is not the lever and the 5.13x mass requirement stands.

prior_claim: Response-guided retry timing was proposed in 2019 and never tested.
search_finding: STILL TRUE, and the selection signal is already published: Vrtovec's responders to a second dose had lower pre-dose LVEF (34.9% vs 40.0%, p=0.02). No trial has used it as an entry rule.
solution: No new molecule and no new device. Take the existing repeat-dose protocol and add an entry rule at the second dose: re-dose only if pre-dose LVEF is below a threshold, and randomise the threshold. This converts an arbitrary calendar interval into a measured decision, and the enrichment arithmetic here sizes it.
primary_endpoint: proportion gaining >=5 pp LVEF after the second dose, guided versus fixed-interval
blockers: The pre-dose LVEF SD is unreported, so enrichment is a swept range; screening failures cost patients and time; the rule needs prospective validation before it can guide care.
falsifier: If enrichment does not materialise prospectively, the Vrtovec subgroup was chance and fixed-interval dosing is as good.

prior_claim: A viability-specific engraftment signal in humans is not done; the animal version needs an engineered reporter gene.
search_finding: OVERSTATED. Human NIS has already been imaged in patients: MV-NIS gave 123I SPECT/CT positives in 8 of 32 myeloma patients and confirmed NIS expression in 3 ovarian-cancer patients across repeat cycles. hNIS is human-derived and expected non-immunogenic, and beat HSV1-tk for cardiac signal and contrast in a direct comparison.
solution: The graft cells are already an engineered allogeneic iPSC line made under GMP, so adding a stable hNIS cassette is a manufacturing change, not a new platform. Image with 123I SPECT/CT or 18F-tetrafluoroborate PET. Both components are individually precedented in humans; the combination in a cardiac graft is not. Protocol: hNIS-tagged versus untagged graft in a small safety cohort, with signal-versus-function correlation as the endpoint, replicating the rodent rho=0.76-0.80 in humans.
primary_endpoint: correlation between day-7 NIS signal and 6-month LVEF change; safety of the tagged product
blockers: Thyroid, stomach and salivary glands express NIS natively, so background must be blocked with perchlorate; reporter silencing over time; a second genetic modification adds regulatory burden.
falsifier: If signal does not track function in humans as it does in rodents, the feedback loop has nothing to close on.

prior_claim: Whether repeat dosing works in humans awaits CATO; nothing to do but wait.
search_finding: STILL AWAITING, but waiting may not settle it. CATO has 20 per arm and two active-versus-control comparisons. At a plausible MRI LVEF-change SD of 6 pp it can only detect roughly a 6 pp difference, and has well under 50% power for the ~3 pp increment the human literature suggests.
solution: Read CATO out as planned, but pre-register the interpretation now: a null result at 20 per arm cannot distinguish 'no effect' from 'an effect too small for this sample'. Pool CATO with the other repeat-dose trials in a prospective meta-analysis, and use the enrichment rule from gap 2 to power the successor trial rather than repeating an underpowered design.
primary_endpoint: CATO: change in LVEF by cardiac MRI at 12 months (already specified)
blockers: Follow-up completes March 2027; the SD assumption drives the power estimate and is swept, not known; pooling needs harmonised endpoints.
falsifier: If the observed between-patient SD is at the low end of the sweep, CATO is better powered than this analysis suggests and the concern is overstated.

prior_claim: The clearance solve needs 2.18x beyond-precedent potency across every module.
search_finding: Partly addressable by architecture rather than potency. ATLAS-2's own ablation found titration worth +72.8 pp, more than any other lever, which implies the potency requirement is substitutable. The trade-off is swept here instead of assumed.
solution: Buy the requirement down with redundancy instead of potency: sweep the potency cap against node and gate redundancy and report the cheapest combination that stays robust. Whatever residual gap remains is the honest specification, and it is smaller than 2.18x if redundancy substitutes at all. Note that VERVE-102 now gives -62% LDL-C from one infusion, which raises the precedented ceiling for the driver module specifically.
primary_endpoint: simulated probability of the clearance target, with the precedent gap stated
blockers: Redundant routes mean more agents, more interactions and more cost; simulation cannot establish that any of these combinations is safe.
falsifier: If no combination below the 2.80x cap is robust, potency is not substitutable and the 2.18x gap stands as written.

prior_claim: A PCSK9-editing outcomes trial is needed; durability is assumed.
search_finding: DURABILITY IS NOW MEASURED. VERVE-102 Heart-2 (NEJM 2026): -88% PCSK9, -62% LDL-C, -78 mg/dL absolute at 1.0 mg/kg, durable to 18 months with 15 participants beyond a year - through hepatocyte turnover of 200-300 days. No dose-limiting toxicity. Still no outcomes data.
solution: Power the outcomes trial on the measured 78 mg/dL rather than a guess. That is 2.02 mmol/L; on the CTT slope it implies a hazard ratio near 0.61, which needs on the order of 130 events - a few thousand patient-years, not a mega-trial. Sweep the slope down to half effect so the design survives being wrong. Randomise editing versus continued standard lipid lowering in established coronary disease.
primary_endpoint: MACE on hard endpoints, editing versus standard care
blockers: The CTT slope is an assumption imported from statins, not an editing result; irreversible editing demands long safety follow-up; the highest dose cohort has the shortest follow-up.
falsifier: If the event curve does not separate on the assumed slope, the surrogate-to-outcome translation fails for editing - which is precisely what the trial is for.
